original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Exhibit one rational rank-one solution of R+S+T+U=4I-E-F-G, for every triple of distinct old projectors, on which all four targets are subset sums, and record that this solution fails the inherited odd-c count.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian native alphabet. This package stays in the abelian symmetric 2-by-2 model and answers the three-old length-7 support question left open by the two-old witness, for one explicit solution rather than a new alphabet.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the signed-frame escape. Support holds for this length-7 witness, but the witness fails the inherited odd-c count, so there is no local call-count saving and no selected-frontier change.
stop_rule: Stop after one explicit seven-label support witness, its carrier case split, and its odd-c count. Do not classify other solutions, and do not search for four odd-c labels.
evidence: Witness: A, B, P, Q, (1/2)A, (3/2)A, and 2B are positive-semidefinite rank-one frames summing to 4I because (1/2)A+(3/2)A=2A and P+Q=A+B=I. Every target is exactly the corresponding projector pair. Every choice of three projectors as old calls leaves four rank-one added frames. Odd c detects P and Q only, against four targets. The inherited inequality is not reproved. This is one solution, not a census.

open_questions.question: Does any other solution of R+S+T+U=4I-E-F-G meet support and also have at least four labels of odd c?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This length-7 witness meets support and fails the inherited odd-c count, so it is excluded as a word. A different solution that meets both tests would be shorter than the eight-call minimum. The same odd-c question for the length-6 equation R+S+T+U=4I-E-F stays with PR #7100 and is a different equation.
open_questions.first_step: Find one other solution of the length-7 equation whose labels have integer c and at least four odd values, then repeat the carrier scan.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package does not classify the solutions of the length-7 equation.
